en: The Uṣṇīṣavijayā Dhāraṇī:
Namaḥ bhagavate tathāgatāya... (Homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata...)
*Vidyā*, the most supreme; *Buddha*, the Great Awakened One; *Bhagavat*, the World-Honored One.
The above constitutes the first section: the Gate of Reverence for the Virtues of the Honored One. *Tadyathā*, meaning "namely" or "as follows."
This is the meaning of what is now spoken: *Oṃ*. The meaning of the Unseen Uṣṇīṣa of the Three Bodies.

The above is the second gate: the Mirror-like Manifestation of the Dharmakāya. *Viśuddha-viśodhaya*, purify; *sam-sam-sam-pada*, universally illuminating; *vibhava*, pervasive radiance; *sphara*, spreading and pervading; *ga-ti-ga-ha-na*, the sixfold dense forest; *svabhāva-vi-nir-mukta*, naturally pure.

The above is the third section, the Gate for Purifying Evil Destinies: *A* *Bi* *Sin* *Tsa* *Du* *Mam*. Empower me! *Su-gata*, Sugata; *Bhara-bhara-tsa-na*, O you of supreme instruction; *Amṛta-bi-ri-kai-ma-ha-mantra-pa-nai*, the nectar of immortality.

Furthermore, it is said: "The Immortal Syllable of Empowerment: Ā HA RA Ā HA RA. May you graciously accept, accept, accept! Recite this three times. To dispel all suffering and affliction: Ā YUṢAṂ DHĀRAṆI, may there be firm abiding and the upholding of longevity.
The above is the fourth section, clearly elucidating the gate of empowerment (*abhiṣeka*).
*Śūddhaya śūddhaya gaganasvabhāva uṣṇīṣa-vijaya-viśodhani* [As pure as] space, purified;
O Uṣṇīṣa, Victorious One, Purifier. *Vi-ja-ya vi-śo-dha-ni*.
Namah samantabhadra-sarva-tathāgata-śāsanānupālaka-sahasra-raśmi-pramukta-saṃcodana-parama-viśuddha-sādhaka.
*Ṣaṭ-kāra-lava-ḍa-pa-ri-bhu-raṇi-sarva-tathāgata-gatānaya-dhiṣṭhāna*
Bhūṣaṇavajra! Adorned by the empowerment of the spiritual power of all Tathāgatas, through the mudrā of Mahāmudrā, may the vajra of the mind be established. Saṃhata-nama-viśuddhe!
O you who are purified by the name of the gathered [assembly]! Vajra! Diamond!
The hook-chain body is pure: *sambhara-nabha-prayā-nṛtya-patari-viṣṭha*.
This is the purification of all obstacles.
These are the karmic obstacles (*karmāvaraṇa*), the retributive obstacles (*vipākāvaraṇa*), and the afflictive obstacles (*kleśāvaraṇa*).
"Attaining purity," and so forth.

The above is the fifth section, the Gate of Empowerment through Spiritual Power (*adhiṣṭhāna*). *Brahmā-dvi-ṇi-vra-ta-rya-a-yuḥ-vardhana-sarva-pāpa-śodhani* (Purifier of All Faults Increasing the Life Span). *Samyak-siddhi-te* (Vow-Empowerment). *Maṇi-maṇi-ma-ha-ma-ṇi* (Jewel of the World; also called the Jewel of the Dharma).
These are the two types of provisions: merit and wisdom. The above concludes the sixth gate, the Increase of Life Span:

*tathāgatapada-guṇa-pāri-nirvṛti-tathatā-bhūtakoṭi-vyāpi-viśuddhi*. *viśva-ṭha-mud-de* manifests the purity of wisdom: *jaya jaya vijaya vijaya vijaya vijaya*. "Victory, victory" is the dharma-gate of the two truths, the ultimate and the conventional. *samarasamarasamara*: maintain this through the union of mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom.
The above is the seventh gate: the Correspondence of Samādhi and Prajñā.
Namaḥ samantabuddhānām. Homage to all Buddhas. Namo vipaśye tathāgatāya.
Homage to the Tathāgata Vipaśyin. Namaḥ śikhine. Homage to Śikhin.
Namaḥ śikhine tathāgatāya. Homage to the Tathāgata Śikhin.
Namovaiśravaṇāya tathāgatāya. Homage to the Tathāgata Vaiśravaṇa. Namo karakūṭasunirmitāya. Homage to Karakūṭasunirmita.
Namaḥ kāruṇikāya namo 'rhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya. Homage to the Compassionate One; homage to the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened One.
Namaḥ krakucchandāya tathāgatāya. Homage to the Tathāgata Krakucchanda. Namaḥ kanakamunaye tathāgatāya.
Homage to the Tathāgata Kanakamuni. Namaḥ... (The remainder of the text follows).
Namaḥ kāśyapāya tathāgatāya. Homage to the Tathāgata Kāśyapa.
Namaḥ śākyamunaye tathāgatāya. Homage to the Tathāgata Śākyamuni.
*Āryāvalokiteśvara-śrī-vajra-pūjita-pariśuddha-adhiṣṭhāna* (Homage to the Noble Avalokiteśvara,
the Vajra Honored by the Pure Empowerment).
Bandha-vajra-bandhara-vajragarbha-vajradṛḍha-siddhi-mama.
(Mama means "mine," used here to state one's own name.)
When performing it for another, one should utter that person's name.
The above is the eighth Vajra Offering Gate: ŚRĪ LAM SARBWA SARBATWA NAN TSA KA YA PA RI.
Vīḍa | Svabhāgatyapariśuddha | Sarvatragaviśuddhasvabhāvatām | Saṃ 3. [The syllables] Vīḍa:
the bodies of all sentient beings attain purity. Svabhāgatyapariśuddha: all destinies are completely pure.
Sarvatragaviśuddhasvabhāvatām: the state of the nature of purity pervading everywhere. Saṃ: three.
*Gamaḥśvāsāyantu sarvasattvān trāyasva samam aviśvasthaṃ tiṣṭha | All Tathāgatas,
comfort them and cause them to attain [peace].*
Adhiṣṭhāna muḍiye muḍiye vī muḍiye vī muḍiye | vibodha vibodha vardhaya vardhaya vī vardhaya vī ||
Vṛ-dha-ya, which causes awakening; that which enables sentient beings to quickly attain awakening.
Sam-bha-bha-ri-ṭṭhe, universally pure. Sarva-tathā-gata-ghra-na-ya-di-sta-na-di-sti-ta, empowered by the spiritual power of all Tathāgatas. Ma-hā-mu-drā. The Great Seal.
This is what is called the Great Seal (Mahāmudrā) of the Tathāgata.
The above concludes the ninth chapter, the Gate of Universal Realization and Purity. *Svāhā*—the auspicious syllable.
Furthermore, it speaks of the meaning of accomplishment (*siddhi*).
The aforementioned tenth section is the "Gate of Accomplishing Nirvāṇa. The Master says:
"This dhāraṇī exists in nine versions in total."
These were the Tripiṭaka Master Du Xingkai Yuezhao,
the Tripiṭaka Master Yijing,
and the Tripiṭaka Master Buddhapālita Shanwuwu.
The versions translated by the Tripitaka Master Vajrabodhi, the Tripitaka Master Amoghavajra, and others,
as well as the commentary by Fachong.
These are the Sanskrit manuscripts transmitted by the Great Master Kōbō Daishi and others. Among them,
we now present side-by-side the Sanskrit manuscript of Kōbō Daishi and the Chinese transliteration with added characters translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Vajrabodhi.
This Sanskrit manuscript was that which Kūkai received from Acharya Huiguo during his stay in Tang China;
it consists of palm-leaf folios upon which the Sanskrit names of the Seven Buddhas and Avalokiteśvara were inscribed.
This differs from other Sanskrit manuscripts;
later generations recognized this.
*Buddhoṣṇīṣavijaya-dhāraṇī*. The second year of Kenkyū (1191), the *xin* year.
